A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SatDreamer360, the same VIGOR++ dataset construction, and matching core experiments. Text, equations, figures and tables support comparison. The supplied v1 ends with references despite mentioning an appendix; v2 includes readable Appendices A.1–A.12.

before.justification: Tables 1–4 report original generation experiments, an attention ablation, and downstream localization results using synthetic training data.

after.justification: The original empirical results are retained, with additional reconstruction and panorama-boundary measurements, component ablations, resource measurements and qualitative experiments.

M1.justification: The loss, triplane representation, dynamic ray attention, epipolar constraint and sparse frame querying remain unchanged. However, Appendix A.5 newly describes temporal 3D-convolution modules in the decoder and their separate training. The PDFs do not establish whether these are an architectural addition or previously undocumented implementation details.

E1.justification: CVUSA, VIGOR, VIGOR++ and downstream localization coverage are retained. Appendix A.4/Figure 9 adds an explicitly tested scenario involving different trajectories generated across batches, conditioning subsequent generation on previously generated images. This modestly extends the tested conditioning scenarios.

E2.justification: The quantitative baseline sets in Tables 1–2 remain unchanged. Figure 4 adds ControlS2S to the qualitative comparison on retained trajectory examples; v1's corresponding comparison included EscherNet but not ControlS2S, although ControlS2S appeared elsewhere.

E3.justification: Section 4 adds LRCE for panorama-boundary consistency and a Pi3 reconstruction/rendering protocol evaluated with 3DPS and 3DSS. Appendices A.6–A.8 introduce controlled component comparisons and specified runtime/memory evaluations, including 10-, 20- and 30-frame sequences. Existing dataset splits and main training settings are retained; newly disclosed training details do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: Tables 5–9 add dedicated tests of triplane versus BEV representations, ray-based versus standard attention, dynamic sampling refinement, and sparse versus dense interframe attention, including resource scaling. Figure 9 adds a cross-batch consistency case study. These substantially expand analysis beyond the retained full-cross-attention versus epipolar-attention comparison.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The additional results retain single-point reporting.

E6.justification: Existing numerical entries in Tables 1–4 are retained. New results include SatDreamer360's 3DPS/3DSS of 13.31/0.5196, LRCE of 14.53 on CVUSA and 5.081 on VIGOR, and the ablation/resource outcomes in Tables 5–9. These are additional findings, not improved scores over v1. Table 6's CVUSA label conflicts with its proposed-method values matching the VIGOR row in Table 2, leaving that comparison's dataset attribution uncertain.

T1.justification: Appendix A.3 adds a derivation of the existing epipolar constraint, using skew-symmetric products in Equations 9–15. The original constraint and main equations remain unchanged; Appendix A.2 restates the existing projection mapping. The added derivation leaves depth-scale factors implicit when identifying inverse projections with 3D points.

C1.justification: The title, abstract and conclusion narrow the framing from continuous ground-view video to multiview-consistent panoramic sequences. The contribution statement also specifies adaptation of epipolar attention to panoramic equirectangular projections and describes the triplane as adopted. The central framework, dataset contribution and superiority claims remain.

C2.justification: New discussions explain cross-batch inconsistency, the importance of vertical triplane information, dynamic sampling refinement and noise from distant frames. Appendix A.9 adds concrete limitations: road-network coverage, nearly identical outputs below 8 m pose separation associated with 15–20 m training spacing and limited triplane resolution, and slow inference. These materially qualify v1's broad continuity and applicability claims.

D1.justification: Appendices A.4–A.5 substantially expand implementation documentation with image-to-triplane attention, batch sizes, sequence lengths, warm-up and fine-tuning schedules, AdamW with learning rate 7e-5, and temporal-decoder training for 40 epochs. Section 3 clarifies feature summation and offset initialization. A new reproducibility statement promises code and dataset release, but supplies no release access.

R1.justification: The introduction, related work and method now explicitly credit prior epipolar-attention and view-synthesis research, including He et al., Tseng et al. and EpiDiff, positioning the contribution as an extension to panoramic imagery. Additional triplane, panorama-metric and reconstruction references broaden the discussion. This substantially revises the positioning of a central claimed contribution.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, method explanations and model analysis receive extensive rewriting, with a pervasive shift from temporal/video terminology to multiview terminology. The title changes, and the document gains a reproducibility statement and a structured appendix covering explanations, experiments, limitations and disclosures.

P2.justification: Tables 1–2 gain metric columns and Tables 5–9 are added. Figure 4 is reorganized and gains ControlS2S rows; retained satellite/trajectory panels move to Figure 10 with relabeling. Figures 8, 9 and 11 add a projection illustration, cross-batch demonstration and further comparisons. Typography, headings and page layout also change substantially.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses substantial gaps in component validation and reproducibility through dedicated ablations, geometry and boundary evaluations, detailed training documentation, and concrete failure conditions. These make the retained performance claims considerably easier to assess. Table 6's dataset inconsistency and the depth-scale ambiguity in the added proof weaken specific additions, but do not outweigh the broader gains in evidence, transparency and appropriately qualified claims.
